Maria Galka called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. with the recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance. The meeting
was held at the Hobart City Court at the PCC Building, 705 E. 4 Street. The change of venue and call-in number
for the zoom connection was available and listed on the agenda, the website and posted on the front door of Hobart
City Hall, 414 Main St. Members in attendance in person: Stuart Allen, Lloyd Emig, Dan Schultz, Mark Kara,
Maria Galka, Dave Vinzant, Kreg Homoky and Alex Metz, City Engineer. Member absent: Matt SeDoris. Also in
attendance: Building Official Felix Perry; Zoning Administrator Connor Miller; Recording Secretary Joy Respecke;
and Plan Commission Attorney Dave Westland.

Present and speaking on behalf of the petitioner was Rich Piazza, Krull/Abonmarche, 111 E. 3r Street, requesting
preliminary approval for Crosby Creek at Carother's Bayou and the subject address is 286 & 300 W. Old Ridge
Road. Proposed is to combine the 2 parcels together into 1 lot. Each parcel has a house and garage located on them
and demolish the house on the 300 Old Ridge Road property and keep the garage. In order for the garage to remain,
the 2 parcels will be combined into 1 parcel. A 15' utility drainage easement is shown around the perimeter on the
east, north and west, a 20' utility easement along the frontage, an area along Old Ridge Road will be dedicated and a
proposed conservation easement for the existing waterway will be shown on the final plat. It is unsure of the exact
language for the eascment and will work staff prior to final plat approval. Ms. Galka opened the public hearing for
Petition 26-08. Ms. Bowman, 266 W. Old Ridge Road is a neighbor and has no issue with the proposed subdivision.
Hearing no further public comments, Ms. Galka closed the public hearing. Mr. Metz felt the conservation easement
should be a minimum of 20' and is a standard subdivision. Mr. Allen motioned to Grant Preliminary Plat Approval
for Petition 26-08 including all discussion, seconded by Mr. Homoky. All ayes, motion carried. (8-0)
Ms. Galka called for the next three items on the agenda: Petitions 26-12, 26-16 and 26-17 and informed the
petitioner that the Public Hearings would be conducted at the same time for these three petitions as they
pertain to the same property and project and advised Attorney Todd Leeth to address each of the three in his
presentation.

Present was Attorney Todd Leeth on behalf of Hobart Owner LLC regarding the east side of the proposed data center
site just south of 61s Ave. Attorney Leeth provided proof of publication as required and noted as part of the public
hearing requirements, a sign is to be posted on the property at least 10 days prior to the public hearing and that it was
brought to his attention prior to the meeting that the sign was not present which was the subject of some discussion
amongst the community. He provided 2 time-stamped photographs as proof the sign was placed on the property on
April 20" and the photo was submitted to the city attorneys.
As to the rezone petition 26-16, Attorney Leeth explained there are over 700 acres of M-1 zoned property south of
615 Avenue, showing a. The T-shaped parcel, he thought to be the extension of Arizona Street, has been vacated and
was the subject of a memorandum of understanding between the city and his client on a land swap. When the
surrounding property was originally rezoned in January of 2025, this small T-shaped parcel was not intended to part
labor is also being utilized at the site who have their own safety policing and protocols on the job-site.
City Engineer Alex Metz noted the plans were reviewed by his staff and the engineering team from Butler, Fairman
& Seufert who provided three sets of comments and revision requests to the plans that have been completed. The
comments remaining are minute only pertain to the buildings themselves, requesting extra details. The drainage,
environmental and traffic have been addressed and traffic will be reviewed on a weekly basis as the project progresses.
Comment wise the plans are technically sound and the plans include a reduction in the site runoff of herbicides and
chemicals from farming materials and the stormwater plans are advantageous to the site and to the surrounding area.
Mr. Metz stated the City is requiring a third party inspection on-site to assure the requirements of the plans are being
met. In addition there are infrastructure agreements that Colorado Street will be repaired after construction, the
extension of water lines down Colorado to 69ạẠạAve. to allow for domestic water for future use and to extend sanitary
sewer down Colorado Street to serve the public in the future, all of which will be paid for by the developer.
Building Commissioner Felix Perry stated the safety and evacuation of the site is the responsibility of the General
Contractors who will also have a nursing/first aid station on-site, manned during working hours. In addition the City
will be hiring a third party construction management company that will serve as inspectors on behalf of the City at the
site and will provide coordination between the contractors, the City and to address any concerns that may arise during
the construction of the project.
There being no further comments or questions, a motion was made by Mr. Homoky, seconded by Mr. Vinzant to grant

Todd Huntington, Langan Engineering, stated there is a lot of continuity between this site proposal and the previous
one granted under Petition 26-12 as the two owners worked together to assure the continuity at to aesthetics and from
a utility standpoint, a site standpoint, the future roundabout, traffic, etc. were done in concert with each other. He
noted that the project anticipates a full build-out of the campus but this portion of the project (Phase 1) is presented
tonight consisting of 9 data center buildings and 3 ancillary buildings on this site and that is the petition for
consideration this evening. In addition, there are ongoing discussions with the City regarding the widening of
Colorado Street in the future and the bike path area is tentative until the amount of right-of-way dedication for
Colorado St. is determined. He noted the right-of-way will be on the east side of Colorado to allow for the widening,
not on the west side and the water main and sanitary sewer extensions will also be part of the right-of-way to be
designed for future construction and paid for by the developer. Taps will also be provided for those properties on the
west side of Colorado when the extensions are constructed. Mr. Huntington reviewed the site plan for phase 1,
showing the berm that extends along 61s Ave. as well as south on Colorado St. He pointed out the class 1 agricultural
wetlands that are currently being reviewed by the Army Corps of Engineers and IDEM on the north and west areas of
the site to get those classified before any work is done in that area. The campus is designed around those areas. Silt
fencing and security fencing is placed on the site well outside of the required wetland buffer areas. The berm shown
will be between 12'-18' high and will tie into the berm on 61s Ave. and run south along Colorado St. The setback
from the right-of-way to the face of the building is 570 feet on 61s Ave. and 470 feet on the Colorado Street side.
There is a temporary primary entrancę to this site off of 61" Ave. with a secondary entrance off Colorado Street to

system for treatment. He noted the 14 million gallons of water per year will not be used and discharged at the same
time but only as needed and with the evaporation, the capacity will allow for the water discharges needed to the
sanitary system. Mr. Kara stated the water tanks on site will hold sufficient gallons so as not to affect the water
pressure and Mr. Eckhart agreed that the water pressures will not be affected. Ms. Galka questioned whether there
was any activity on the site that would affect the water table. Mr. Eckhart stated the water experts have stated there
is no dewatering on the site except for localized sump pumps that may be used during utility burial construction. Mr.
Perry asked for a description and purpose of the three ancillary buildings on the site. An Amazon representatives stated
there is an auxiliary water building that houses the fire pumps and water pumps for both the domestic water and the
industrial cooling water for the campus and for water storage on site to not impact the water pressures. He noted that
the average water consumption per year is 14 million gallons with almost 3 million gallons of storage on site. City
Engineer Alex Metz stated there is also an agreement in place for the water storage and use with Indiana American
Water and the storage should be more than sufficient to handle the needs of the project. Mr. Perry and Ms. Galka
asked how the generator testing times and run times are distributed and the AWS representative stated there is a 6
minute bi-weekly generator test for each generator. He noted that testing will be spaced over 6-8 hours each day, none
on the weekends.
There being no further comments or questions, a motion was made by Mr. Homoky, seconded by Mr. Vinzant to grant
Site Plan Approval to Petition 26-14 as prescnted. City Engineer Metz stated there will be third party inspectors on
site on behalf of the City during the construction and there are some concerns regarding the storm water overflow
calculations. Phil Gralik, Butler Fairman and Seufert, the City's consulting engineer, stated that the calculations show
that some ponding may occur on roadways and the swale shown may need some adjusting and they are working with
the AWS consultants to address those concerns and finalize the design adjustments to meet the City Standards. Mr.
Homoky amended his motion to include the contingencies that there will be 3rd party inspectors on site and that the
drainage and swale design shown be redesigned to meet the City Standards, Mr. Vinzant agreed and amended his
second to the motion with the added contingencies. Roll Call Vote taken. All aye, motion carried. (8-0)
Motion by Mr. Vinzant, seconded by Mr. Schultz, to grant preliminary plat for a 1-lot subdivision under Petition 26-
18 contingent on having a 40' right-of-way along Colorado Street being shown on the preliminary plat and including
findings of fact as presented. Roll Call Vote taken. All aye, motion carried. (8-0)
Consultation/Discussion: There being no further comments or discussion Mr. Schultz motioned to adjourn,
seconded by Mr. Homoky. All aye, motion carried. (8-0) Meeting adjourned at 11:15 p.m.
